_doc: Roster + bare-agent + OpenClaw config for sinain. This is the single
source of truth for everything agent-shaped:
- top-level fields  → bare-agent infra (poll, turns, tool whitelists)
- escalation block  → routing policy (was ESCALATION_* in .env)
- analyzer block    → loop pacing (was AGENT_DEBOUNCE_MS / _MAX_INTERVAL_MS)
- profiles          → one entry per CLI binary or routing target
(claude, openclaude, codex, ..., openclaw)
This is the COMMITTED example. The actual file run.sh and sinain-core
read is sinain-agent-runner/agents.json (gitignored). On first run, run.sh
copies this example into agents.json so a fresh checkout works without
manual setup. sinain-core falls back to this file too if agents.json
doesn't exist yet.
Path resolution in sinain-core: AGENTS_CONFIG_PATH env override, or
default: <repo-root>/sinain-agent-runner/agents.json (resolved relative to
the sinain-core/dist directory).
Profile fields (all optional except `type`):
type      Determines dispatch path AND CLI flag layout.
Local CLIs (HTTP-dispatched): claude, openclaude, codex,
goose, junie, aider — bare agent invokes the binary.
Gateway profiles (WS-dispatched): openclaw — sinain-core
sends via WS RPC. Multiple gateway profiles with different
names are allowed (e.g. nemoclaw, nanoclaw-prod) — any
profile with `type: "openclaw"` is treated as a gateway.
All gateway profiles auto-register in the overlay roster.
bin       Path or name of a real binary on PATH (default: profile
name). Shell aliases are invisible here — replicate them
as bin (the underlying binary) + env (the vars the alias
was setting). See the pclaude example.
settings  Path to a Claude-Code-style settings.json (default:
sinain-agent-runner/.claude/settings.json — the hook-bearing one).
model     OPENAI_MODEL override (only meaningful for openclaude /
CLAUDE_CODE_USE_OPENAI=1 paths).
env       Per-profile env overrides applied only for this binary's
invocation. Values may use ${VAR} indirection (anywhere in
the string) to read from the parent shell's environment —
keep secrets in .env, not here.
openclaw-profile-only fields (consumed by sinain-core):
wsUrl, wsToken, httpUrl, httpToken, sessionKey, phase1TimeoutMs,
phase2TimeoutMs, pingIntervalMs
Examples beyond the built-ins live under `_examples`. Move any of them
into `profiles` to activate; the runtime ignores keys it doesn't know.
escAllowedTools: ${allowedTools} Bash(git:*) Edit Write Read Glob Grep LS
spawnAllowedTools: ${allowedTools} Bash(git:*) Edit Write Read Glob Grep LS
autoApproveTools: Read Glob Grep Ls Cat Edit Write MultiEdit NotebookEdit WebFetch WebSearch TaskCreate TaskUpdate TaskGet TaskList TaskOutput TaskStop LSP Skill Monitor BashOutput KillBash mcp__sinain* ToolSearch

escalation._comment: Lane (the agent picked for escalation in agents.json `default` or via the overlay chip) is the source of truth for whether escalation runs. `mode` is intentionally omitted here — the runtime default (rich) applies, and registerBareAgent reconciles mode with lane at boot. Override `mode` only if you want to force selective/focus/off semantics.

sinain._comment: Sinain's OWN bundled chat agent — a RESIDENT OpenHands sidecar (sinain-chat-agent/) on ws://127.0.0.1:9610, NOT a run.sh subprocess. Fast non-reasoning model (qwen3.5-flash, reasoning off) + lean sinain tools + token streaming → sub-4s responsive chat. type 'sinain' routes the chat/escalation lane to the sidecar via sinain-core's ChatService. The CHAT and TERMINAL lanes are DECOUPLED: sinain is the chat `default` and appears only in the chat roster; it is EXCLUDED from the terminal roster (no interactive TUI). The terminal lane has its own `terminalDefault` (openclaude) and its own selection.

openclaude._comment: Routes through the local OpenRouter proxy (auto-launched on :11435 by run.sh) → DeepSeek V4 Flash. Proxy preserves reasoning_content across multi-turn MCP flows. To use Anthropic API directly, drop the env block (or just pick the `claude` profile).

openclaw._comment: OpenClaw gateway routing. Move this entry into `profiles` to enable. The wizard's `sinain onboard --advanced` step or `sinain config gateway` populates this section automatically with your gateway URL/tokens. Selecting openclaw for a lane sends that lane's traffic via WS RPC to the gateway instead of the local bare agent. Disabled by default so first-run installs don't attempt WS connections to a gateway that isn't running.

pclaude._comment: Personal claude config. `bin` must be a real PATH binary — replicate a shell alias as bin+env (the alias `pclaude=CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=$HOME/.claude-personal claude` becomes the entry below).

pclaude-with-personal-endpoint._comment: Personal claude pointing at a private OpenAI-compat endpoint.

openclaude-spawn._comment: Different settings.json for the spawn lane vs the escalation lane.

openclaude-gpt5._comment: Same binary, different model + key for a different OpenRouter route.

nemoclaw._comment: Server-side NemoClaw (or any openclaw-fork) on a different host. `type: openclaw` makes it a WS-dispatched gateway alongside the canonical openclaw profile. Currently, only the first gateway profile gets a live WS client at startup — selecting nemoclaw in the overlay routes via WS, but the connection still uses openclaw's URL until per-profile WS clients ship.
